**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

The MFN rule is satisfied at the **preferred** position: this Master Services Agreement imposes no most-favoured-nation or terms-parity obligation on AP at all.

- I reviewed the full document (single section, p0000–p0074) and ran targeted searches for "most favored nation", "no less favorable", "favourable", "third party terms", and "best" — none surfaced any parity, best-pricing, or offer-matching covenant in either direction.
- Section 5 (Fees and Payment, p0023) defers revenue sharing to individual Exhibits without any undertaking that AP will give Kubient terms no less favourable than those given to others.
- Section 1 (p0001) actually runs in our favour, confirming the arrangement is non-exclusive and that AP remains free to offer Inventory via other agents or sell to third parties — the opposite of an MFN burden, and therefore not something to flag.

One diligence note carried in the rationale rather than as a deviation: the fee Exhibits referenced in Sections 1 and 5 are not attached to this document. If any Exhibit or order form introduces a rate-matching or parity covenant in Kubient's favour, it should be re-tested against this rule.
